title: Bluepine Logistics on-prem inference scratchpad
content:
Notes from kickoff + followups (rough)

Context: Bluepine Logistics wants on-prem inference inside their US-EAST datacenter (air-gapped segment). Pilot scope: customer-facing ETA/FAQ assistant for ops and shipment reconciliation (initially text generation + embeddings for searching internal docs). Primary constraint is strict network controls & hardware heterogeneity.

Call highlights 2026-03-05 w/ PM + infra (A. Gomez, L. Chen):
- Pilot target: 6-week PoC, production-ish SLA after successful validation. Pilot deadline: 2026-04-30 (hard ask from customer finance).
- Latency SLO: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 500ms for short chat queries (~<64 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state ~20-30 rps, with occasional bursts to 60rps (end of month batch queries).
- Data: PII + logistics manifests. Must remain on-prem; logs to be retained for 90 days in-house. Customer wants HSM/KMS integration for model keys (AES wrapping via their Vault cluster).
- Hardware inventory (customer provided): 4x NVIDIA A10G (shared across teams), 1x A100 (isolated), 2x CPU-only nodes (for control plane); no NVLink across the A10G nodes; NFS-backed storage (SAS, 12k IOPS nominal but currently noisy).

Immediate technical gotchas / risks:
1) Air-gapped artifact flow: customer requires signed container images & offline model artifact transfer. Need to validate our offline packaging workflow (tarball + sha256) — DO NOT rely on public registries.
2) Quantized model artifacts: customer wants to save memory but insists on reproducible outputs for audits. Our 4-bit quantized 13B variants may drift; need eval harness comparing float16 vs quantized at their exact tokenization and prompt sets.
3) Tokenizer mismatches: Bluepine uses legacy byte-level tokenizer in some pipelines. Must standardize on single tokenizer at inference entrypoint (tiktoken vs legacy). Action: add tokenization shim to gateway to normalize.
4) KV cache eviction + concurrent sessions: A10G memory may be tight if we run multi-tenant; continuous batching behavior could hold KV memory; plan capacity for worst-case concurrency.
5) Storage I/O bottleneck: NFS can spike latency and stall model mmap. Consider local SSD scratch + periodic sync to NFS for embeddings/index files.
6) Model fallback policy: customer asked for cheaper fallback for non-sensitive queries (7B quantized). Need routing rules in gateway and clear audit trail for which model served which request.
7) Observability: customer wants per-request token-level cost breakdown and redaction rules for PII before logs leave the cluster.
8) HSM/KMS: integration requires a KMS plugin to our control-plane agent (customer uses Vault with PKCS#11). Need dev-time access to a Vault test cluster.

Notes on performance expectations / tests to run:
- Microbench: single-token generation latency on A100 vs A10G for their 13B model replica; target p50 < 10ms per-token on A100 (estimate).
- End-to-end: cold-start vs hot cache; run 5k queries from their sample prompt set (mix: 60% sub-64 token, 30% 64-256, 10% >256). Capture p50/p95/p99 and tail jitter.
- Batching experiments: continuous batching helps when qps bursts >15rps; with 20-30rps expect batch sizes 2-6 depending on arrival pattern. If arrival is bursty, might still meet latency SLO via prioritization for low-latency route.
- Embeddings indexing: Faiss on local SSD (recommended) vs NFS – index build memory spikes; need swap/oom safeguards.

Security / compliance checklist (customer asks):
- Air-gap artifact ingestion process doc (we must provide step-by-step).
- HSM/KMS + key rotation policy for model keys.
- Audit log filter spec (PII redaction rules).
- Data retention and deletion workflow (90-day retention + secure purge).

Open questions to chase (owners assigned):
- Can infra give us a dedicated A100 for the pilot (Ravi) — current ask: isolate inference box for latency-sensitive route. (Owner: Ravi Menon)
- Does Bluepine allow short-lived egress to our signing service for image verification? If not, need a fully offline signing and transfer workflow. (Owner: Sanjay Rao)
- Which tokenizer variant is canonical inside their ETL? Get sample tokenized outputs for 10 prompts. (Owner: Elena Fischer)
- Who is Bluepine security contact for PKCS#11 access + test vault? (Owner: Maya Patel)

Action items (short):
- [Maya] Draft air-gap artifact transfer doc + signed-image checklist (due: 2026-03-14).
- [Sanjay] Spin up offline packaging demo (tar+sha + instructions) and validate on local VM (due: 2026-03-18).
- [Elena] Run tokenizer sync test with their sample prompts, report token counts and mismatches (due: 2026-03-12 — overdue, nudging).
- [Ravi] Capacity map: produce rough sizing table (nodes, RAM, GPU memory headroom, expected concurrency) and propose local-SSD vs NFS layout (due: 2026-03-17).
- [All] Prep short perf-run checklist and test harness repo (link in linked_artifacts once created).

Conversation snippets / quick quotes:
- "We absolutely cannot have PII leave the air-gapped segment." — Bluepine sec lead
- "If we miss the April timeline finance pulls funding until Q3." — Bluepine PM

Risks / mitigation summary:
- Risk: Quantization causes audit/regressions -> Mitigation: run side-by-side eval & keep float16 rollback path with routing policy.
- Risk: NFS I/O spikes kill latency -> Mitigation: local SSD caching + pre-warm indexes, IO throttling.
- Risk: Tokenizer mismatch yields hallucination on canonical prompts -> Mitigation: tokenize normalization at gateway + include tokenizer-specific tests in eval suite.

Potential POC config (non-final):
- Control plane/agents (k8s control plane in their air-gapped cluster; we run a small control agent VM per node).
- Inference plane: dedicated A100 node running float16 13B model for latency-sensitive route; 2 A10G nodes hosting quantized 13B/7B variants behind fallback.
- Storage: local NVMe for model shards + NFS for long-term artifact archive.
- Observability: Prometheus + node-exporter local, logs to internal ELK stack with redaction layer.

Customer messaging draft (for next sync):
- Quick summary of pilot scope, what we need from them (dedicated A100?, Vault test creds, permission for one-time artifact egress or acceptance of signed tarballs), and timeline with milestones.

Next call proposed times: 2026-03-16 or 2026-03-19 (prefer morning PST).

Misc scratch notes:
- Check license for certain CUDA/driver versions with their older distro (RHEL 7.x variant?)
- Ask infra to validate NUMA setup on A10G nodes; memory pinning could matter for mmap'd weights.
- Keep audit trail that records which model variant served each request (for quality/regression debugging).

Bottom line: doable in pilot window but need early decisions on image transfer and dedicated A100. Prioritize offline packaging demo + tokenizer sync immediately.
